title: Artificial intelligence and firm-level productivity
explain_beginner: This study looked at whether companies that use artificial intelligence become more productive. The researchers surveyed German firms and compared those using AI with those that did not. They found a clear positive link: firms using AI tended to have higher productivity, and this held whether they simply adopted AI or used it more intensively. The authors took extra care to rule out the possibility that already-successful firms are simply more likely to adopt AI. This matters because it suggests AI may genuinely help businesses produce more, not just appear modern.
explain_business: This paper offers evidence that AI adoption is linked to higher productivity at the firm level, based on German survey data rather than vendor marketing. The researchers used careful statistical methods to reduce the chance that the result simply reflects already-strong firms adopting AI. The finding holds for both whether a firm uses AI and how intensively it does so. For executives, this supports treating AI investment as a plausible productivity lever, while noting the evidence is associational and based on German firms. It informs decisions about whether to pilot or expand AI in business processes.
explain_practitioner: The authors used unique firm-level survey data from Germany on AI adoption and estimated productivity effects. They analyzed both a cross-sectional dataset and a panel database. Because AI adoption may be endogenous, meaning more productive firms might self-select into adoption, they applied instrumental variable estimators alongside standard approaches. They tested two AI measures: a binary adoption indicator and the intensity of AI use in business processes. Both measures showed positive and statistically significant associations with firm productivity. The editor notes this survey-based IV evidence is more credible than vendor case studies relying on self-reported benefits.
